newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 9.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - According to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, the first proposal from Finance Minister Ivan Pilip for budget cuts is for a bit less than 25 billion crowns. The chairman of the Christian Democrats and Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux and Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka confirmed that plans for total budget cuts are between 40 and 60 billion crowns.

- HSBC, which is authorised to organise the entry of a strategic partner into Agrobanka, reduced the choices to three companies. Among these should be Raiffeisenbank, which together with Agrobanka owns AR Stavebni Sporitelna, and ING Bank.
- From June 16, the fifth largest Czech brewery, Jihoceske Pivovary, is increasing its prices by 60 to 80 crowns per hectolitre, 60 to 80 hellers per litre.

- According to a spokesman for the Czech National Bank, Martin Svehla, the foreign banks with which it is meeting over an one-year syndicated credit include Chase Investment Bank Limited, Commerzbank AG, J.P. Morgan Securities and SBC Warburg, a branch of Swiss Bank Corporation.

- Due to the situation on the financial market, Daewoo increased the prices of its models Nexia (by 20,000 crowns) and Pico (by 10,000 crowns). Renault increased its prices by an average of six percent.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The chairman of the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) and Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux said it is absurd to think that some representatives of his party would not support the cabinet during the confidence vote to be held in parliament.

- The Czech Medical Chamber proposes doctors be paid only for the amount of hours which coincide with common work hours. This is to prevent repeating situations where doctors charge insurance companies for 20 or even 30 hours of work a day.
- In the next week, parliament should definitively finish the investigation into the causes of the insolvency of Kreditni Banka Plzen.
- Despite current economic problems, the union of school workers wants to continue to push for an increase in wages.
- The trade deficit with Russia increased during the first four months of this year to 12.2 billion crowns, one billion more than from January to April last year.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - During a meeting with the cabinet on Saturday, the Czech-Moravian union federation assured Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus that unions are not preparing protest actions.

- At a meeting of the Free Democrats and the National Socialist Liberal Party (SD-LSNS) on Saturday, the two factions, liberal and national socialist, could not agree on the future of the party, and liberals announced they were leaving the party.
- The largest domestic yarn maker, Vlnap Nejdek, had losses last year of 28.755 million crowns with revenue of 729 million crowns.
- Jihoceska Plynarenska had net profits last year of 36.651 million crowns, from which it will pay dividends only on employee shares, while the remainder, 33.123 million, will be invested.
PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel wants to use his right to participate in cabinet meetings. He claimed that after he took office in 1993, Klaus' cabinet informed him that meetings are internal affairs.
- President Vaclav Havel said on Sunday that he thinks it is legitimate to discuss delaying this year's deregulation of rents and energy prices.
- Praga a.s. ended last year with profits of 62.082 million crowns. It will use the profits to cover losses from 1994 and will not pay dividends.
